pip.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: preview-only single-mascot design study with a quiet tutoring UI context.
Create realistic, production-quality UI designs with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, and purposeful spacing. This is ONE mascot concept, not a comparison grid.
User direction: After Class is a personal learning app. User loves isometric tactile objects and a tiny after-school world, but tutoring and learning must remain the focus. Mascot will be one selectable skin. Companion stays small and calm in real use, with restrained motion. No grades, XP, streaks, mastery meters, score confetti, giant mascot chat bubbles, or rewards. It is a curious peer, not a teacher.
Target dimensions 1536 x 1024 landscape design board. Single cohesive concept. No browser/device chrome, no photo mockup framing, no watermark. Current date anchor November 3 2026 America/Los_Angeles; show no dates.
Composition: warm ivory paper page with very generous space. Header small "After Class", then the exact mascot name prominently and a short style subtitle. Left 42% shows ONE large beautiful three-quarter isometric mascot portrait on a tiny piece of desk or book, for inspecting its design. No busy illustrated room. Small label "Character study". Right 58% shows one restrained front-on lesson surface labeled "In a lesson", where the SAME character is only 64–80px tall in the outer bottom margin. This actual-use size is critical. Large readable tutor question, quiet answer space, minimal controls. Text verbatim in lesson: "Locks & deadlocks", "Why might two threads wait on each other?", "Start with what you remember…", "Speak", "Share my thinking", "Hint", "Source". No conversation or speech bubbles from mascot. Use warm serif for question/header and clean sans-serif for UI, maximum two fonts; readable 16px body. Simple spacing and light dividers, not dashboard widgets/cards inside cards.
Mood: collected, warm, curious, adult-friendly, not childish or hyperactive. Mascot resting/listening, mouth closed, low-key expression; readable silhouette at 64px; minimal accessories, no weapons, exaggerated glittery eyes, magical particle clouds, giant grins or background clutter.
References attached are visual inspiration, not edit targets: Colorfigures washer image for fine ink outlines, precise four-tone dimensional solids, mint/cobalt/coral palette and geometric cast shadow; Tinycharts Saturday image for miniature inhabited warm-paper spatial charm. Do not reproduce those objects or webpage. Honor the particular style and character description below.
Mascot name (verbatim): "Pip"
Subtitle (verbatim): "The eraser friend"
Character: a small rounded rectangular cream rubber eraser creature, coral-red top quarter as a fitted cap, tiny black dot eyes on the cream front, two little cobalt feet, short cream arms resting on its knees. A single narrow ochre book strap across its body; no bag clutter. Same character as the eraser companion in the attached prior After Class concept, refined into a strong simple silhouette. Slightly rounded corners, subtle rubber grain, softly beveled edges, four-tone solid shading, fine imperfect ink contours, navy cast shadow. Seated on a closed mint pocket notebook, gently leaning forward to listen. Warm, forgiving, thoughtful expression. Materially tactile isometric hand-inked object, not shiny plastic or flat emoji.
The lesson preview should be almost all readable neutral paper, mascot tucked in the lower left margin; the miniature world is only the little notebook it sits on. Keep coral to this small accent. Tiny footer "Quiet company for thinking."
